text:
alex: seeing a surge of healthy traffic pinned to us-west even though latency-based routing should have steered ~30% to eu-west. user reports and grafana traces line up. looks like sticky routes for ~10m at a time :/

sam: yup, we've got SNAT connection counters spiking on us-west NATs + connection timeouts to backend pools. logs show conntrack evictions. sample: `conntrack: table full, dropping packet`

jin: digging into DNS side — our GeoDNS provider returns eu-west for ~35% of queries but client resolvers are holding old answers. suspect negative caching/TTL mismatch between our authoritative TTL (30s) and some ISP resolvers honoring higher values. doing a dig from a bogon resolver:```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short @8.8.8.8 service.redwood.ai
35.214.10.11
;; Query time: 12 msec
```

maya: ugh. so even if we change routing quickly, caches mean traffic sticks. that explains SNAT pressure — traffic concentrated in us-west for longer windows.

alex: any evidence the fallback policy is exacerbating it? we have region pinning set for 60s with fallback to nearest with capacity.

sam: our fallback kicks in, but because the resolver keeps returning the pinned IP set, the client never fails over to the fallback endpoints. client-side retry logic is per-request, but DNS pins the egress path.

jin: quick note: some of our customers use long-lived DNS TTLs in their internal forwarders. even if we drop TTL to 5s, it won't help those resolvers.

maya: proposed mitigation sequence: 1) temporarily increase fallback aggressiveness (lower probe thresholds) so server-side can reject/redirect quicker, 2) bump DNS TTL to 10s and advertise change, 3) add an egress-level redirect header for newer clients that follow 307 to fall back region. thoughts?

sam: +1 on lowering probe thresholds. set probe_failure_threshold=2, probe_interval=5s for 10m window? that would make the routing layer consider a region unhealthy faster. but risk of flapping.

alex: to avoid flapping, we can add a short holdoff (grace window) where once demoted we keep it demoted for 30s. that plus hysteresis should reduce oscillation.

jin: I'll start the DNS TTL change, but will add a note to support page asking customers to clear caches if they run local forwarders. changing upstream provider settings now: `ttl: 10` -> pushing.

deploy-bot: deploy started by jin: geo-dns/ttl -> 10s (canary 1/10). CI: passed, rolling.

maya: rolling the fallback tweak to canary on beta routing group. config snippet:```yaml
routing:
  failover:
    probe_interval: 5s
    failure_threshold: 2
    demote_holdoff: 30s
```

sam: monitoring wise i'll add dashboards: nat_conntrack_evictions, regional_egress_qps, probe_fail_count. also add an alert for nat_conntrack_evictions > 10/min.

alex: cost note — if we spread traffic to eu-west more, egress costs might increase ~8% for this week. let's flag finance for visibility.

maya: copied finance@gold into the incident thread.

jin: canary of ttl and failover rules applied. early telemetry shows eu-west share up to 28% (was 6%). conntrack drops down on us-west.

sam: nice. keep an eye on flaps — currently stable. i'll keep the stricter probe settings for 2 hours then relax to production values with demote_holdoff still in place.

alex: action items: jin -> monitor DNS propagation and post ISP holdouts, sam -> alerts + rollback plan, maya -> create PR to make demote_holdoff configurable per region, alex -> ping finance.

maya: thanks all. follow-up in #eng-platform after 2h or sooner if anything odd. :thumbsup:
